stem: Which statement about immunisation and egg allergy is correct?

options.text: Food allergies such as egg allergy are usually okay
Egg allergy always requires avoidance of all vaccines
Egg allergy means all vaccines must be given only in hospital
Egg allergy means vaccines can be given only after mixing with local anaesthetic
Egg allergy changes the recommended injection site from thigh to forearm

explanation: Food allergies such as egg allergy are usually okay. Egg allergy does not usually mean routine vaccines should be withheld.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Adverse Events Following Immunisation; National Immunisation Schedule and Immunisation for Special Populations

optionExplanations.A: Correct because food allergies such as egg allergy are usually okay and do not usually require withholding routine vaccines.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because egg allergy does not always require avoidance of all vaccines.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because egg allergy does not mean all vaccines must be given only in hospital.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because vaccines should not be mixed with local anaesthetic, and egg allergy does not change that.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because egg allergy does not change the recommended injection site; site selection is based on age and vaccine type.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
